switch_table_family_REFUSED.verdict: NOT takeable by a marker plan. The refusal is STRUCTURAL and is a SECOND WALL, distinct from the marker gate: it is not that the shim declines to place markers, it is that the positions built puts them at DO NOT EXIST in the derived body.
switch_table_family_REFUSED.the_wall: `canon_markers` numbers blocks by a DFS preorder over RAW successors. Built's `match` lowering interposes one 0-assign `falseEdge` candidate block per arm (two for an or-pattern), and its `if` lowering interposes a 0-assign else-entry block AND an empty join block. The shim's `lower_ir_to_mir` emits one MIR block per trust-ir block and has none of them, so every marker at or after an arm sits at a different FINE index. No marker plan can move it: a plan chooses WHICH markers to place, not what the block graph is.

the_change.note: the three compiler files register the `cf-post-late` perturbation CLASS with the driver's option domain and change no emission; without them the sealed driver rejects the control flag at parse time and the perturbation cannot be run at all.
parts: CfPostOp — the three measured post-op forms
plan_call_fwd_markers — the block splits at THE call, not at the last node; the post region is validated instruction by instruction

call_fwd_source_admits — the HIR peels the post-op and must ANSWER the same form the trust-ir witnessed; the FIELD form additionally requires a NON-SCALAR call return, which is what makes MfTy::Opaque a checked token rather than a guess
predict_call_fwd — the slot opens first, carries the class's FIRST use-site key (Some((1,0,0)) for the two operand forms, none for the field form), and retires one assign into the successor

the emitter — the destination temp is minted before the argument temps, the call is routed into it, and the retirement is DEFERRED to the Return arm (the only deferred marker in the shim, because the post-op's write happens one node later)
ShimCx::mf_call_fwd_post_route — the post-op's own result goes STRAIGHT into `_0`, wave-J's move for a directly-returned call result, plan-gated

two_refusals_the_first_two_whole_crate_r: run 1 — all eight bodies went `agreed -> unsupported`, marker law, line 0: predicted `mk b0.0:live s0:Usize@term` vs derived `mk b0.0:live s0:Usize@b1.0:0`. Cause: the post-op destination temp is read by an ASSIGNMENT, so the observed side keys it; wave-CF registers no keys because its temps are moved by the call TERMINATOR. Fixed by registering the key.

run 2 — the three FIELD bodies converted; the five operand bodies refused at line 3: predicted `mk b1.1:dead s0` vs derived `mk b1.2:dead s0`. Cause: the shim gives every non-call instruction result an `mf_result_temp` and the Return arm copies it, so the successor carried TWO assigns where built carries ONE. Fixed by wave-J's own move — route the post-op's result straight into `_0`, plan-gated.
